1

The petitioner has filed this petition U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident that occurred on 13.01.2023.
2.

The petition averments in brief are as under:
On 13.01.2023 at about 12.45 a.m., the petitioner along with his friend were travelling in a passenger autorickshaw bearing No. KA-02-AF-3750 and when they reached near Vengalappanahalli, Magadi- Bangalore main road, Magadi at that time the driver of Ashok Leyland bearing No. TN-30-AR-6088 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner with high speed and dashed against the autorickshaw.
Due to the said impact, the autorickshaw turtle and the petitioner fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Govt. Hospital, Magadi and after first aid he was shifted to Unity Life Line Hospital wherein he was admitted as inpatient and has spent more than Rs.3,00,000/- towards hospitalization charges,
treatment medicines, conveyance, nourishing food and other incidental charges etc.,

Prior to the accident, petitioner was very hale and healthy and he was doing private work and earning Rs.20,000/- p.m. Due to the accidental injuries petitioner is not able to continue his work and is under complete bed rest and he is suffering from permanent disability.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle,
are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

Hence,
prays to award compensation of Rs.16,00,000/- with interest.
3. After service of notices, respondent No.1 remained absent hence, placed exparte.
Respondent No.2 appeared through its counsel and filed written statement by denying the issuance of policy to the Ashok Leyland goods vehicle bearing No. TN-30AR- 6088.

Further contended that,
the accident was happened due to negligence on the part of the driver of autorickshaw who was driving the said vehicle in a rash and negligent manner. Also contended that the driver of the offending vehicle was not having valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident and also without valid permit in the said route.
Further denied the age, avocation, alleged disability and income of the petitioner.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive and exorbitant.
Hence, the respondent No.2 prays to dismiss the petition against it.

4. On the basis of the rival contention, the following issues are framed by this court:
1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries due to the actionable negligent driving of lorry bearing No. TN-30-AR-6088 by its driver, in RTA took place on 13.1.2023 at about 12.45 a.m. on Magadi-  Bangalore main road, near  Vengalappanahalli, Magadi Taluk,
Kumaraswamy B.C vs Moorthy.K on 15 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152244959/
2  Ramanagara?
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount and from whom?

3 . What Order or Award?
5.
In order to prove the claim petition, the petitioner examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to 11.
Dr. N. Chaitanya Babu who is working as Dental Orthopaedic Surgeon is examined as PW.2, through him got marked Ex.P12.
In spite of sufficient opportunities, the respondents did not chose to adduce evidence.

6. Heard the arguments of both sides and perused the material evidence that are available on record.
7.
My findings on the above issues are as under.

Issue No.1 : In the affirmative;
 Issue No.2 : Partly in the affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final orders  for the following:-
 : R E A S O N S:
 ISSUE NO.1 :
8.
That by reiterating all the averments made in the petition, the petitioner has filed his affidavit in lieu of- examination in-chief, which is considered as P.W.1.

In support of his case, he has produced true copies of FIR, complaint, spot mahazar, wound certificate, indemnity bond and charge sheet,
which are marked under Ex.P.1 to 6.
9.
On perusal of Ex.P1- FIR is registered on the basis of Ex.P2 first information given by one Ramanna who is the father of the petitioner.
After the registration of FIR as per Ex.P1, the Ex.P3 spot mahazar was conducted.

It is the main allegation is that, the Ashok Leyland bearing No.
TN-30-AR-6088 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner suddenly changed his lane and dashed against the autorickhsaw in which the petitioner was proceeding.
The IO has conducted spot mahazar and as per the mahazar there is a divider in the accident spot.

The driver of offending vehicle bearing No. TN-30-AR-6088 instead of going in his left side of the road by crossing the divider came in the right side of the road and d ashed against the autorickhsaw in which the petitioner was proceeding.
This itself established the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.

The learned counsel for the respondent No.2 at the time of cross-examination of PW.1 even though tried to make out the negligence on the part of the driver of the autorickshaw, the answers of the PW.1 and also the contents of mahazar establishes the negligence on the part of the driver of offending vehicle bearing No. TN-30- AR-6088.

The driver of offending vehicle bearing No. TN-30-AR-6088 instead of proceeding in the way it is meant for to go towards Magadi came to Kumaraswamy B.C vs Moorthy.K on 15 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152244959/
3 the wrong way by crossing the divider which is meant for the vehicles which goes towards Bangalore.

Thus, the prime negligence is on the part of the driver of offending vehicle bearing No.
TN-30-AR-6088.
No other grounds are made out to hold the negligence on the part of the driver of the autorickshaw.
10. After conducting spot mahazar as per Ex.P3, the IO subjected both the vehicles for IMV inspection.
As per the contents of IMV inspection report marked at Ex.P10, the offending vehicle bearing No. TN-30-AR-6088 has got damaged in its front side and left side.
This also supported the case of the petitioner regarding the actionable negligence by the driver of offending vehicle bearing No. TN-30-AR-6088.
If the Ashok Leyland bearing No. TN-30-AR-6088, has not came in the wrong side, it is not going to be damaged in its front and left side.
The contents of Ex.P10 helped the case of the petitioner.

11. Ex.P6 charge sheet is also came to be filed on the driver of the Ashok Leyland bearing No.
TN-30-AR- 6088, the IO has opined that the negligence is on the part of driver of the Ashok Leyland bearing No. TN-30- AR-6088.
No other grounds are made out by the respondents to show the contributory negligence from the petitioner.
12. The respondent No.2 has filed written statement by denying the negligence and their liability.
But both the respondents have not lead any evidence to rebut the case of the petitioner.
As discussed supra, the petitioner successfully established the actionable negligence by the driver of offending vehicle bearing No. TN-30-AR-6088.

Thus, by considering all these points this court is of the opinion that the said accident is caused by the rash and negligent driving by the driver of offending vehicle bearing No. TN-30-AR-6088.
13.
The first respondent who is the owner of the offending vehicle does not chosen to deny the allegation of the rash and negligence driving.
The respondent no.2 even though filed written statement, has failed to establish the negligence on the part of autorickshaw.

The respondent No.1 &
2 even after sufficient opportunity have not lead any evidence to disprove the contents of these documents.

The charge sheet is came to be filed on driver of offending vehicle bearing No.
TN-30-AR-6088 for the offences punishable under Sec. 279, 337 & 338 of IPC.

sentences.text: Proceedings under Motor Vehicles Act are not akin to proceedings in a Civil Court.
Hence, strict rules of evidence are not required to be followed in this regard.

14. In a claim for compensation under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision reported in 2011 Kumaraswamy B.C vs Moorthy.K on 15 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152244959/

sentences.text: The claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.
15. The contents of Ex.P3 spot mahazar and Ex.P10 IMV report falsifies the contention of respondent no.2 about the contributory negligence of driver of autorickshaw for the occurrence of accident.

In this context by considering the contents of Ex.P1 to 6 this court tilts in favour of the petitioner as the petitioner has to prove the alleged negligence on the basis of the evidence and proof of the same on preponderance of probabilities.

The Ex.P6 charge sheet also supports the view of this court, as the charge sheet filed for the offence punishable under Sec. 279,337 & 338 of IPC against the driver of Ashok Leyland bearing No. TN-30-AR-6088.
16.

The learned counsel for respondent No.2 has taken a contention that there is a delay of one day in registering the FIR as such, the case of the petitioner has to be considered as suspicious and created one.
In this regard, if we perused the contents of Ex.P2 & 1, the alleged accident is in the mid night 1.30 a.m. of 13.1.2023 and case is came to registered on 13.1.2023 at about 5.30 p.m.
Further at the time of drawing of mahazar as per Ex.P3 on 14.1.2023 at about 10.00 a.m. the IO has found the marks of the accident and also blood stains in the accident spot.
As per Ex.P4 the petitioner admitted to the hospital at around 12.45 a.m. of 13.1.2023 with the history of getting injuries in road traffic accident at about 12.10 a.m. on 13.1.2023.
Thus, these documents shows that soon after the accident, the petitioner admitted to the hospital for treatement and there is no inordinate delay in registering the FIR.
17. As per well settled principle of law, the standard of proof in the claim petition like the present is preponderance of the probability.
There are no grounds to disbelieve the case of petitioner in the absence of rebuttal evidence.

All the materials available on record leading to show that, petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident took place on 13.1.2023 which is caused by the driver of Ashok Leyland bearing No. TN-30-AR-6088, which belonging to respondent No.1.
There is no reason to discard the evidence of petitioner.

In the claim petition like present one strict proof is not necessary,
but preponderance of probabilities is sufficient.
Accordingly, issue No.1 answered in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.2:
18.
As already held herein above, the petitioner has proved that he has sustained injuries in RTA which is caused by respondent No.1.
Hence, the petitioner is entitle for compensation.
Now the quantum of compensation is to be ascertained on different heads.

a) PAIN AND AGONY :- At the time of alleged accident the petitioner was aged about 39 years.
Aadhaar card produced at Ex.P11 shows the date of birth of the petitioner as 15.12.1983 hence, as on Kumaraswamy B.C vs Moorthy.K on 15 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152244959/
5
the date of accident petitioner was aged about 40 years.

In the petition itself he has averred that he was admitted to Govt. Hospital, Magadi and after first aid he was shifted to Unity Life Line Hospital,
Bangalore.
As per the discharge summary marked at Ex.P7 the petitioner sustained fracture nasal bone with mobile anterior tooth in the upper jaw.
He underwent closed reduction of nasal bone fracture on 13.1.2023.
By considering the nature of the injuries and period he spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident Rs.35,000/- may be awarded to the petitioner under this head.
b) Medical expenses:
The petitioner has produced medical bills as per Ex.P11, amounting to Rs.53,533/-.
These bills are not disputed by the respondents and no grounds are made out to disbelieving these bills.
Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case in combined with the alleged injuries the petitioner is entitled for the reimbursement of the same by rounding of the same i.e., Rs.53,600/-.
c) Loss of income during laid up period:
The petitioner has stated that he was doing private work and earning Rs.20,000/- p.m.
To prove the said fact the petitioner has not produced any document.
Such being the case, it is just and necessary to consider the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.16,000/- p.m. as the accident is of the year 2023.
As per the discharge summary marked at Ex.P 7- the petitioner was admitted to Unity Life Line Hospital for 3 days.

Thereafter usually the healing period has to be considered for which in the absence of evidence, this court is of the opinion that in total two months period including 3 days inpatient period may be considered under this head as a loss of income.
So, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.16,000 X 2 months = Rs.32,000/- during the laid up period.

d) Disability;- To prove the nature of injuries sustained by him the petitioner examined Dr.
Chaitanya N. Dental Surgeon as PW.2, through him X-ray is marked at Ex.P.12.
According to the evidence of this witness the petitioner sustained pan facial injury.
The petitioner has physical orofacial disability and disfiguration i.e., fracture of nasal bone and mobile anterior tooth in upper jaw.
He examined the petitioner for assessment of disability.
Petitioner suffered whole body disability at 15%.
This aspect is not impeached during the course of cross-examination.
Further PW.2 has also stated that the petitioner requires replacement of left mandibular canine with implants.
The evidence of Pw.2 reveals that the petitioner has got permanent disability in respect of his three teeth and also the functions of jaws has got disturbed.
The evidence of PW.2 also reveals that the petitioner ability to bite hard food will be restricted to 50% only.

Even though the evidence of PW.2 states that the disability of the petitioner in respect of whole body is at 15%, we need to consider the effects of the alleged factors on the working life of the petitioner.
The disability in respect three teeth are permanent.
The functions of the jaw is not like earlier.
The petitioner lost the ability of chewing hard food.
This will certainly make the petitioner to have soft food and his food habits are going to be changed.
By this, when the capacity of intaking of food reduces, certainly it will effect the functional ability of the petitioner.

Thus, by considering the same the functional disability of the petitioner is assessed to 12% by holding that the alleged injuries will certainly effects his functional Kumaraswamy B.C vs Moorthy.K on 15 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152244959/
6 ability.
According to the petitioner he was doing private work.
The disability caused to the petitioner may affect on his occupation to some extent.

Hence, I hold that the petitioner sustained disability of 12%
to the whole body.
The petitioner has produced his Aadhaar card marked at Ex.P11, as per this document the date of birth of the petitioner is shown as 15.12.1983.
The accident was occurred in the year-2023.
So, as on the date of the accident the petitioner was aged 40 years.
As per Sarala Verma's case, the proper multiplier applicable to the age of petitioner is '15'.
Hence, I inclined to award future loss of income at Rs.16,000/- X 12 X 15 X12% =Rs.3,45,600/- which is the total loss of future income.
e) FOOD, NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE ;
As per Ex.P7 discharge summary, the petitioner took treatment as inpatient for a period of 3 days.
As per wound certificate marked at Ex.P4 the injuries sustained by the petitioner are grievous and simple in nature.
The disability in respect three teeth are permanent.
The functions of the jaw is not like earlier.
The petitioner lost the ability of chewing hard food.
This will certainly make the petitioner to have soft food and his food habits are going to be changed.
By considering the nature of the injuries and period he spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident.
Hence looking to the treatment taken by the petitioner and injuries sustained he is entitled for compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards food and nourishment and conveyance.
f) ATTENDANT CHARGES:
The petitioner sustained grievous injuries in the accident.
The petitioner has spent 3 days in the hospital and there is no evidence or pleading in this regard to show that the petitioner is in need of attendant.

But by considering the nature of the fracture as discussed above, it may be considered to award attendant charges at Rs.1,000/- per day i.e.,
Rs.3,000/- in total as the petitioner has spent 18 days in the hospital.
g) Towards loss of amenities and enjoyment of life:
The disability in respect three teeth are permanent.
The functions of the jaw is not like earlier.
The petitioner lost the ability of chewing hard food.
This will certainly make the petitioner to have soft food and his food habits are going to be changed.
The petitioner admitted to the hospital for the injuries sustained by him, which might certainly have deprived him of the basic comforts and enjoyment.
Therefore, it is just and proper to award a reasonable sum of Rs.40,000/- under this head.
h)Towards future medical expenses: PW.2 stated that the petitioner requires replacement of left mandibular canine with implants.
By looking to the nature of injuries sustained the treatment taken, the petitioner is entitle for Rs.25,000/- under this head.

Kumaraswamy B.C vs Moorthy.K on 15 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152244959/
7

Thus, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
a) Towards pain and agony Rs. 35,000/-
b) Towards medical expenses Rs. 53,600/-
c) Towards loss of income Rs. 32,000/-
d) Towards disability Rs. 3,45,600/-

e) Towards food, nourishment  and conveyance Rs. 20,000/-
f) Towards attendant charges Rs. 3,000/-
g) Towards loss of amenities Rs. 40,000/-
h) Towards future medical  expenses Rs. 25,000/-
 _______________
Total Rs
19. Liability:-
According to the petitioner the respondent No.1 & 2 are the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle.
The respondent No.2 in its objection statement has denied the issuance of policy to the Ashok Leyland bearing No. TN-30-AR-6088.
But the learned counsel for the petitioner has produced copy of insurance policy of the said offending vehicle.
As per the said document the insurance policy was in force as on the date of accident.

Hence,
the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner and the respondent No.2 insurance company shall indemnify the compensation on behalf of the respondent No.1.
The petitioner is entitle for compensation with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., Accordingly, this issue answered partly in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.3:
20.

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
Kumaraswamy B.C vs Moorthy.K on 15 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152244959/
8 O RDE R
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.5,54,200/-
(Rupees Five lakhs fifty four thousand two hundred only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.
The respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.
Considering the quantum of the amount awarded, it is ordered to release the entire compensation amount to the petitioner.
Advocate fee is fixed at 1,500/-.
Draw up award accordingly.
